baselines.name: Prange information-set decoding
baselines.problem: Syndrome decoding of a linear code: find a low-weight error, or a word satisfying many parity checks, from a parity-check matrix and a syndrome.
baselines.summary: Choose a random information set, solve the parity checks on it by Gaussian elimination and keep the candidate when the remaining coordinates have low weight or satisfy enough checks; repeat. The generic decoder any quantum decoding, DQI or Gibbs-sampling route must beat. The referenced notes match product-USD quantum decoders with Prange-style classical samplers and measure BPQM against the Prange rank ceiling.

baselines.name: Information-set decoding with pinning and Fourier enumeration
baselines.problem: Syndrome decoding and learning parity with noise when plain Prange restarts are too slow: the error is spread over a small block that can be enumerated.
baselines.summary: Fix (pin) a few coordinates of the error, then enumerate a small block of it, or score every candidate on that block at once with a Walsh-Hadamard or F_p fast Fourier transform: Stern and Dumer information-set decoding, and the transform step of BKW-style LPN solvers. A better exponent than plain Prange, so it is the fair comparison when a quantum decoder has only been measured against Prange.

baselines.name: Best-of-N Prange completion
baselines.problem: Optimal polynomial intersection and max-LINSAT over a prime field: make as many constraints as possible land in their accepted sets with one low-degree polynomial or codeword.
baselines.summary: Pick n independent constraints, draw a target from each one's accepted set, solve for the codeword by Gaussian elimination mod q and count how many other constraints land in their accepted sets; keep the best of N restarts. The finite-length counterpart of the Prange line rho + (1 - rho) n/m that a DQI margin is measured against. The DQI screener (tools/dqi_screen/screen.py) computes that asymptotic line and the Theorem 10 restart length, not a best-of-N score; prange_restarts in tools/dqi_screen/prange.py computes the best-of-N score on an instance, given its matrix, accepted sets and q.

baselines.name: LP decoding of cycle codes
baselines.problem: Decoding cycle codes (codes whose checks are the vertices of a graph), the codes DQI reduces Max-Cut and Max-k-Cut with two-variable constraints to, including q = 3 colouring codes.
baselines.summary: Relax maximum-likelihood decoding to a linear program and round its solution; polynomial time. arXiv:2609.40036 shows LP decoders recover a positive fraction of randomly located errors with arbitrary values on regular logarithmic-girth graphs and uses them to bound DQI with classical decoders. Run it before claiming a DQI or BPQM edge on a cycle or colouring code.

baselines.name: Quadratic-extension norm search
baselines.problem: Prime-field optimal polynomial intersection with mixed square and non-square (quadratic character) coset constraints.
baselines.summary: Factor a target polynomial over F_p and F_{p^2} to write it as a norm from the quadratic extension (a monic polynomial is a norm exactly when every odd-degree irreducible factor has even multiplicity); the norm gives a polynomial within the degree budget that meets the mixed square and non-square constraints. Standard factorization and norm machinery. In the referenced note it solves both saved N127, K77 mixed inputs perfectly; it does not reach the K39 inputs under its degree budget.

baselines.name: Power completion by formal r-th roots
baselines.problem: Prime-field optimal polynomial intersection whose constraints ask Q(a_i) - t_i to lie in the r-th powers (common-coset power-character predicates).
baselines.summary: Interpolate the selected shifts, take the polynomial part of the r-th root of a padded polynomial in the formal series at infinity, and correct, so that Q(a_i) - t_i is an r-th power at every selected point. Solves every common-coset input perfectly when K >= (r - 1) ceil(N / r); at lower rates it forces about rK / (r - 1) constraints.

baselines.name: Polar successive-cancellation source shaping
baselines.problem: Sampling the Gibbs law of a signed parity-check objective on a polar code (uniform random signs), the task a polar or BPQM quantum Gibbs sampler would solve.
baselines.summary: Sample the dual source distribution one polar coordinate at a time by successive cancellation, conditioned on the frozen syndrome; O(N log N) per sample. On explicit non-prefix half-rate polar sets it reaches average-sign total variation at most 0.010221 at N = 32768.

baselines.name: USD-Prange rejection sampler
baselines.problem: Gibbs sampling of signed XOR (parity-check) Ising models that a quantum decoder built on unambiguous state discrimination would prepare.
baselines.summary: Dequantize a USD-based quantum decoder: erase each symbol or block with the USD failure probability, solve the surviving parity constraints by Gaussian elimination as in Prange, and accept or reject; it matches the decoder's temperature threshold (arXiv:2610.03566). The block version in the referenced note eliminates the inner spin of each parity block and matches the collective triple decoder's erasure and rank condition.

baselines.name: Algorithmic stochastic localization
baselines.problem: Sampling Gibbs distributions of disordered spin models (mean-field spin glasses, the quantum p-spin model) at temperatures where a quantum Gibbs sampler is efficient.
baselines.summary: Follow the stochastic localization process, estimating the mean of the tilted distribution at each step; this reduces sampling from a distribution on the hypercube to mean estimation. arXiv:2609.40250 uses it to sample typical quantum p-spin Gibbs states to polynomially small total variation in (almost) polynomial time.

baselines.name: Tensor-network simulation
baselines.problem: Classical simulation of quantum circuits and many-body dynamics with limited entanglement: shallow or 1D circuits, gapped ground states, short times.
baselines.summary: Represent the state as a network of small tensors (MPS, PEPS) and contract it; the cost grows with the bond dimension, that is with the entanglement across cuts. The default competitor for a simulation or shallow-circuit advantage. The referenced note's general no-go was retracted; the baseline is the method, not that note's bound.

baselines.name: Belief propagation decoding
baselines.problem: Decoding LDPC and other sparse parity-check codes, and inference from noisy sparse parities, on tree-like factor graphs.
baselines.summary: Pass log-likelihood ratios along the Tanner graph with the tanh rule; exact on trees and close to threshold on sparse random codes. The classical baseline for BPQM and other quantum message-passing decoders, and for noisy-parity bridges built from sparse checks.

baselines.name: LLL reduction with Babai rounding
baselines.problem: Closest-vector and bounded-distance decoding in a lattice: modular subset sum, affine lattices derived from DCP, native ternary records.
baselines.summary: LLL-reduce the basis, then round with Babai's nearest-plane algorithm or coordinate rounding, optionally with small repair menus or a Kannan embedding; polynomial time, and exact when the target lies within the Gram-Schmidt decoding radius. The baseline for any lattice or subset-sum reduction of DCP or ternary decoding.

baselines.name: Groebner basis solving
baselines.problem: Solving multivariate polynomial systems over finite fields: ternary-error equations b = A^T s + e, quadratic (MQ) reductions of character constraints.
baselines.summary: Compute a Groebner basis (Buchberger, F4/F5) or linearize by degree (XL, Arora-Ge style annihilators) and read off the solutions; exponential in the worst case, polynomial when enough equations over-determine the system. The ternary quotient decoder is an implemented instance; the folded-norm MQ solver applies a generic Groebner solver to a native quadratic reduction.

baselines.name: Semidefinite relaxation and rounding
baselines.problem: Max-Cut, Max-k-CSP and other constraint optimization on graphs, the targets of QAOA.
baselines.summary: Solve the semidefinite relaxation and round with a random hyperplane: a 0.878 approximation for Max-Cut (Goemans-Williamson), and optimal for every CSP under the Unique Games Conjecture (Raghavendra). Shallow QAOA on bounded-degree graphs has to beat it, and local classical algorithms, before an approximation advantage is claimed.

baselines.name: Index calculus and subexponential class-group algorithms
baselines.problem: Discrete logarithms, class groups, unit groups and regulators of number fields.
baselines.summary: Collect relations among smooth elements over a factor base, then solve the linear algebra; subexponential in the discriminant for fixed degree (Buchmann, under GRH). The classical competitor for quantum unit-group and regulator algorithms; the referenced note is about the quantum side's dependence on the field degree.
